subject: gr-qc
title_original: Gravitational lensing time delay beyond the Shapiro/geometry split
authors: Luca Teodori, Kfir Blum, Zhaoyu Bai
abstract: Time delays are a key observable in strong gravitational lensing systems. Their theoretical expression is usually written as a sum of a geometrical delay and a Shapiro delay, with cosmology entering through angular diameter distances and a redshift prefactor. In this work we derive this structure from the exact null geodesics of the Schwarzschild-de Sitter metric. The standard formula is recovered as the leading term in a small-angle expansion, and we identify the first correction to the usual geometrical-plus-Shapiro split. Such correction does not introduce any new cosmological dependence: it corresponds instead to a higher-order correction intrinsic to the Schwarzschild part of the metric. As a consequence, up to this order, the cosmological constant enters only through the unlensed angular diameter distances and the unlensed lens-redshift prefactor.
title_relatable: Gravitational lensing time delays: where the standard formula breaks down
hook: A careful derivation from exact geodesics shows the familiar geometry-plus-Shapiro split holds to higher order than assumed, with cosmological corrections entering only through standard distance factors.
summary: The textbook formula for gravitational lensing time delays splits the signal into a geometric path-length term and a Shapiro (gravitational potential) term, with cosmology folded in via angular diameter distances. Starting from exact null geodesics in the Schwarzschild-de Sitter metric, this work derives the first correction to that split and finds it carries no new cosmological dependence — it is purely a higher-order Schwarzschild contribution. The cosmological constant therefore enters time delays only through the standard unlensed distances and redshift prefactor, tightening the theoretical footing for using lensing time delays as a cosmological probe.
